title: List of Note Abbreviations (Print Only)

illustrates.quote: Before the note section in each volume, repeat lists of abbreviations for book/magazine titles referred to in the endnotes. List the abbreviations using 1-3 margins and follow print for punctuation, capitalization, and font attributes. Also follow print for the capitalization and use of font attributes for the abbreviations within the endnote.

blocks.features: Boxed heading 'NOTES' with italic sub-heading 'Abbreviations', above a two-column key: each row is a small-caps/plain abbreviation on the left and its expansion on the right.

print.surroundingText: Explicitly labeled '(Print Only)' in its own title, illustrating the abbreviations-list requirement of rule 16.9.3e; immediately followed by a cross-reference to Sample 16-11: Endnotes on page 16-30.
print.printFeatures: Boxed screenshot of a five-row abbreviations key with a bordered box, heading 'NOTES' and italic 'Abbreviations' sub-heading; no braille shown below it.

braille.notes: Explicitly '(Print Only)' -- the source gives no braille rendering for this example; none is guessed.

resolution: illustrates.rule set to 16.9.3.e per standards-map.md's own BANA §16/B004 §11 worked-examples table (the project's established canonical id), not either run's own guess. print.blocks/print.notes follow Run B's schema ([ref:MARK] tokens inline + a separate print.notes[] array of {ref, placement, text}), matching this task's required schema; Run A instead folded each note's real content directly into a sibling print.blocks entry with no [ref:MARK] markers and always an empty print.notes[] -- a schema-level difference, not a content disagreement. braille.width: explicitly '(Print Only)' in the source; both runs agree. braille.lines: the two runs agreed byte-for-byte; kept as transcribed.
